sections.h2: AI Video Ads vs a Filming Day
paras: Turnaround: you get a version from a photo or a link, while a filming day waits on a person, a place, and a date.
Cost: a filming day bills the day, the person on camera, and the editing after. A version here draws on the plan you already pay for. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits.
Variants: each extra opening is another file from the photo you already have. The product stays the same.
Brand control: you write the line, using the facts on the product page. A hired person has to follow that written line.
Usage rights: the file can sit on the product page and in a paid placement. Ask a hired creator, in writing, where their film is allowed to run.
A shop with many products can reuse one opening on each item that has its own photo. Each item is still its own file.

sections.h2: How Shops Set Up One Test
paras: Run three openings of the same product, and change only the first second. The product stays the product in the photo.
Make one clip from the photo you already have. Do not build a second set.
Keep the same product, and change only the first second between the two files.
If you sell in another country, change the spoken language and keep the same product. The script names only what the product page says.

sections.h2: How to Keep a Small Test Fair
paras: Change only one thing between versions, so the result points at that one thing.
Worth testing, one at a time: the opening, the setting, the shape, the length, and the line you add afterward. Start with the opening. It decides whether anyone sees the rest.
sections.alt: Two hands set a plain white cream jar beside a blank white card.

sections.h2: How the Versions Should Run Together
paras: One campaign gives every version the same audience, the same budget, and the same product page.
Many ad accounts let several ads share one group. Some also split the audience across versions. A version that barely ran has not been tested. Leave the ads alone while the test is live.
sections.alt: Two pairs of hands hold the same plain white cream jar in side-by-side poses.

sections.h2: How to Tell Which Version Works
paras: Wait until each version has actually played before you name a winner.

Read three numbers in order. First, how many people stay past the opening. Second, how often people click. Third, the cost each time someone buys. A version can get more views and still lose on sales.
sections.alt: A hand rests beside a plain white cream jar and a blank white card.

sections.h2: What the Next Test Should Change
paras: Keep the version that brings sales at a cost you can accept. Turn off the clear losers, and change one new thing.
Write down the date, what changed, and the result. When a winner starts costing more per sale, make fresh versions. Work through the opening, the setting, the shape, the length, then the offer.

faq.q: Where do I see which ad version worked?
faq.a: Check your ad account for views, clicks, and sales for each version. The video tool makes the ads; your campaign results show what worked.

faq.q: Can Meta or TikTok reject an AI video ad?
faq.a: Yes. An AI ad can be rejected if it breaks the platform’s ad rules. Check claims and any required AI disclosure before you spend more.

faq.q: Should I change the price in just one ad version?
faq.a: Keep the same price when you are testing a new opening or visual. Test a different price separately so you know what changed the result.

faq.q: How does AI make a video ad?
faq.a: It makes video ads from a product photo, link, or short description. You get a script, presenter, and voice without filming.

faq.q: Do I have to label an AI actor in my ad?
faq.a: Follow the platform’s current disclosure rules when you post. Be especially clear if the video could look like a real customer review.

faq.q: How many ad versions should I test first?
faq.a: Start with a few versions so each gets enough budget to compare. Change one thing at a time, such as the opening, to see what helps.

faq.q: Can I make ads for several products?
faq.a: Yes. Use a photo or link for each product and make versions for your catalog. You can test different products and openings without a new shoot.

faq.q: What if one ad version barely gets shown?
faq.a: Give each version enough exposure before comparing results. If one gets almost no views, you cannot tell whether its opening worked.

faq.q: Which tool should I use to test video ads?
faq.a: Choose one that makes several versions from the same product and lets you change the opening quickly. AIVideosUGC can make those versions without new shoots.

faq.q: Which video sizes can I download for ads?
faq.a: Choose 9:16 for TikTok and Reels, 1:1 for feeds, or 16:9 for wide placements. You can also choose 4:3 or 3:4.

faq.q: How much do AI video ads cost?
faq.a: Videos cost 24 to 120 credits, depending on length. Starter costs $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro costs $35 for 300, and Premium costs $63 for 600.

faq.q: How do I make video ads to test?
faq.a: Start with a product photo or link and make several versions with different openings. Keep the product and offer the same so you can compare results.

faq.q: Can I use AI videos as paid ads?
faq.a: Yes. You can use the downloaded video in paid ads without a watermark or separate actor license. Check that your product claims are accurate before posting.

faq.q: What should I test first in a video ad?
faq.a: Test the opening first because it decides whether people keep watching. Make several short versions from the same product photo and compare them.

faq.q: Do AI video ads work as well as filmed ads?
faq.a: Results depend on your product, audience, and offer. Try both in the same ad account to see which brings more clicks or sales.
